articles.title: Make India global hub for space startups: PM Modi
articles.content: Make India global hub for space startups: PM Modi The Hans India Update: 2026-08-24 03:14 IST Prime Minister Narendra Modi poses during an interaction session with the CEOs and founders of space startups on the National Space Day in New Delhi on Sunday New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday called for policy consistency and a globally competitive ecosystem as he interacted with chief executives of Indian space startups, saying India should aspire to become a destination where talent from across the world comes to build its future. The Prime Minister lauded the entrepreneurs for taking risks in a relatively new sector and for placing their faith in the government following the opening up of India’s space industry to private participation. He said predictable and stable policymaking was crucial to encouraging innovation and giving entrepreneurs the confidence to pursue ambitious ventures. “Whatever decisions we take, we should remain consistent with them and should not keep changing them repeatedly,” Modi said, stressing that those taking risks should feel assured of a supportive policy environment even when they encounter setbacks. The interaction covered a wide range of technologies and ambitions, including launch vehicles, satellite propulsion, orbital services, space debris removal, in-orbit refuelling, ground station networks and pharmaceutical manufacturing in space. A Skyroot representative described the company as India’s first space-tech unicorn and spoke about the July 18 launch of India’s first private rocket, which deployed satellites. Calling the achievement only a “warm-up”, the CEO said it marked the beginning of the company’s larger journey. The company plans to undertake one launch every month by the middle of next year and has already set up three factories with the capacity to manufacture one rocket a month, the CEO said. Its longer-term ambition is to scale up to one launch a week and eventually several launches a day. Modi also sought to know whether the successful launch had improved investor confidence and opened up new opportunities for the country’s emerging private space sector. Startup leaders said investor confidence had increased, while another CEO said the company had secured eight launch contracts in the past month, most of them from international customers. “The world must now be looking for Indian startups, asking who is there in this field. Because once there is a breakthrough, people’s attention immediately turns towards it,” Modi observed. The Prime Minister also highlighted the opportunity to make India a major global hub for space talent. He noted that Indian professionals based in the US and Europe were increasingly seeking to return home and join Indian companies after the sector was opened to greater private participation. “We should create an aura that makes people across the world look to India to build their future,” Modi said, adding that people should see India as a destination for building careers in the space sector. During the interaction, PM Modi praised entrepreneurs for taking risks and venturing into the emerging space sector, while emphasising the need for policy consistency to build confidence among investors and startups. “Whatever decisions we take, we should remain consistent with them and should not keep changing them repeatedly,” the Prime Minister said. The CEO of Skyroot described the company as India’s first space-tech unicorn and referred to its successful July 18 launch of India’s first private rocket, which deployed satellites. The CEO said the launch was only a “warm-up” and that the company aims to undertake one launch every month by the middle of next year. The CEO also said Skyroot has established three factories and has the capacity to produce one rocket per month, with plans to eventually scale up to one launch per week and, subsequently, several launches a day. PM Modi also discussed investor confidence following the launch. One startup CEO said the company had received eight launch contracts in the past month after a single launch, most of them from international customers. Highlighting the global visibility such breakthroughs can create for Indian startups, PM Modi said the world should increasingly look towards Indian companies once they demonstrate capabilities in the space sector. “The world must now be looking for Indian startups, asking who is there in this field. Because once there is a breakthrough, people’s attention immediately turns towards it,” he said. The Prime Minister also stressed the potential for India to emerge as a global hub for space talent and innovation. During the interaction, a CEO said Indian citizens based in the US and Europe were seeking to return and work with Indian space companies following the opening up of the sector. PM Modi said India should create an ecosystem that attracts talent from across the world and encourages people to build their careers in the country. “We should create an aura that makes people across the world look to India to build their future,” he said. An entrepreneur described his company as India’s first space-pharma startup. Another startup representative said the company was planning to take its innovation to 10 lakh farmers. articles.title: India's first 100% indigenised AK-203 'Sher' rifle made, test-fired at factory in UP's Amethi
articles.content: India's first 100% indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifle made, test-fired at factory in UP's Amethi “We have successfully produced and fired the first AK-203 (Sher) rifle made with 100% Indian components and input materials,” IRRPL CEO Major Gen Sharma said. Updated on: Aug 23, 2026, 23:12:56 IST By HT News Desk Prefer HT on Google Share via Copy link India has manufactured and tested a prototype of the 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifle, with army trials for the weapon to begin in September this year, Major General SK Sharma said on Sunday, while sharing a video of the test firing. Ever single component and input material which has gone into manufacturing the rifle is sourced from the Indian industry, Major Gen Sharma said. (LinkedIn/ Maj Gen SK Sharma, AVSM, SM(Bar), VSM) The rifles are manufactured by the Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited, a joint-venture of the Indian Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), along with Concern Kalashnikov and Rosoboron export from Russia. Maj Gen S K Sharma, who is the CEO and managing director of IRRPL, said the testing of the prototype was “a moment of immense pride” for the company. Also Read | Indian Army to get loitering munitions worth ₹ 1,577 crore “We have successfully produced and fired the first AK-203 (Sher) rifle made with 100% Indian components and input materials,” Major Gen Sharma said in a post on LinkedIn. ‘Every single component, input material sourced from India’ Ever single component and input material which has gone into manufacturing the rifle is sourced from the Indian industry, Major Gen Sharma said in the post. He said this was not just “localisation of selected components”, but was a “true, end-to-end ‘100% genuine indigenisation’ of the rifle.” He said the prototype of the first 100 per cent indigenised vehicle had “successfully undergone firing, including burst firing”, adding that the initial results were “extremely encouraging.” “A proud moment for IRRPL, our partners (AWEIL & OSL) and MSMEs, and the entire Indian Defence Industry. This is Atmanirbhar Bharat in action!!” Major Gen Sharma said. Also Read | India imposes phased ban on import of 405 defence items to boost domestic production ‘IRRPL moving towards production rate of one AK-203 every 100 seconds’ Major Gen Sharma said that with the successful testing of the first prototype, IRRPL would now focus on producing the requisite number of 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifles for trials to the Indian Armed Forces in September, 2026. The IRRPL CEO said the company will be “moving towards a production rate of one AK-203 (Sher) every 100 seconds,” adding that there is “much more ahead.” Major Gen Sharma further said that IRRPL was also looking to prepone the delivery timeline of the approximately 6 lakh rifles that it has to supply to the Indian Army “by almost one year”. He credited the company's efforts towards “capacity enhancement, indigenisation and production optimisation” for the efficiency.
